stem: Who is the Constitutional Head of the State Governments?
expl: According to Article 154(1) of the Constitution, the executive power of the State shall be vested in the Governor, who shall exercise it, in accordance with the Constitution, either directly or through officers subordinate to him.

stem: The Governor of a State is appointed by -

options.label: d
options.text: The Chief Justice of the High Court

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / more than one of the above

expl: The Governor of a State is appointed by a warrant under the hand and seal of the President. Notably, Part VI of the Indian Constitution (Articles 153 to 167) describes the State Executive. The State Executive includes the Governor, the Chief Minister, the Council of Ministers, and the Advocate General of the State. The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President. Besides, the Governor may resign at any time by addressing the resignation to the President.

stem: Who appoints the Governor of Jammu & Kashmir?

options.label: a
options.text: The Chief Minister of Jammu & Kashmir

options.label: b
options.text: The Chief Justice of High Court of Jammu & Kashmir

expl: Under Article 370 of the Constitution, the State of Jammu and Kashmir was given a special arrangement different from other States of India as “temporary provisions” under Part XXI. In this context, earlier the head of the executive there was not appointed by the President of India; rather, he was elected by the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly. However, this anomaly was removed in 1965. As a result, the head of the executive in Jammu and Kashmir came to be known as the Governor (instead of Sadr-e-Riyasat), and his appointment began to be made by the President of India. Under the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, from 31 October 2019, the State of Jammu and Kashmir was reorganised into two Union Territories—Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh—where the provision of Lieutenant Governors was made, who are appointed by the President.

expl: At present, the Governor of West Bengal is Dr. C.V. Ananda Bose (since 23 November 2022), whereas the Governor of Gujarat is Acharya Devvrat (since 22 July 2019). (1) legislative Council and Governor
(2) legislative Assembly and legislative Council

(4) Governor, legislative Assembly and legislative Council where it exists
Select your answer out of the following codes-
expl: According to Article 168, the State Legislature includes— (1) Governor (2) Legislative Assembly (3) Legislative Council, where it exists

stem: Which is the Upper Chamber of State legislatures in India?
expl: According to Article 168, the State Legislature may be unicameral or bicameral. In a bicameral legislature, the Legislative Council is the Upper House and the Legislative Assembly is the Lower House.

stem: Which one of the following Indian States has the largest number of members in its State legislature?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In Part VI of the Constitution, Articles 168–212 describe the State Legislature. According to Article 170, each State Legislative Assembly consists of not more than 500 and not less than 60 members elected directly from territorial constituencies. At present, the smallest assembly is that of the Union Territory of Puducherry (30), while among States it is Sikkim (32), and the largest is Uttar Pradesh (403). Among the given options, Arunachal Pradesh (60), Meghalaya (60), and Manipur (60) have the same strength, while Himachal Pradesh (68) has the highest. Therefore, the correct answer is option (b).

stem: The members of a State legislative Council are not chosen by which of the following categories of persons?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above.

expl: Under Article 171(3), the composition of the Legislative Council is provided. It includes 1/3 members elected by local bodies, 1/12 members elected by graduates of at least three years’ standing, 1/12 members elected by persons engaged in teaching for at least three years (not below secondary level), 1/3 members elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly, and the remaining members nominated by the Governor. Hence, members are not chosen from the category of industrialists.

stem: What is the maximum number of members a State legislative Assembly can have in India?
expl: According to Article 170(1), each State Legislative Assembly shall consist of not more than 500 and not less than 60 members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the State.

stem: Which of the following Articles of Indian Constitution consists the provision of the election of legislative Assemblies of States–
expl: According to Article 170(1), each State Legislative Assembly shall consist of not more than 500 and not less than 60 members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the State.

stem: In a State, the legislative Council can be created or abolished by—

options.label: a
options.text: The Legislative Assembly of that State

options.label: c
options.text: The Parliament, on the recommendation of the Governor

options.label: d
options.text: The President, on the recommendation of the Governor

expl: According to Article 169(1), the power to create or abolish the Legislative Council in a State lies with the Parliament. The Parliament can do so when a resolution is passed by the State Legislative Assembly by (i) a majority of the total membership of the Assembly and (ii) a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.

stem:
legislative Council exists in which of the following states?
(1) Kerala (2) Himachal Pradesh

Select your answer from the following codes–
expl: At present, Legislative Councils exist in Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana. Therefore, Legislative Councils exist in 6 States in India.

stem: If the Speaker of legislative Assembly of a State wants to resign, he will give his resignation to –
expl: According to Article 179, the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly may resign his office by writing under his hand addressed to the Deputy Speaker.

stem: To whom the State Council of Ministers collectively responsible?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Under Article 164(2) of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers of a State is collectively responsible to the State Legislative Assembly. Similarly, the Union Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

stem: The Chief Minister of Union Territory, where such a setup exists, is appointed by the

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Chief Minister of a Union Territory shall be appointed by the President, and the other Ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the Chief Minister, and the Ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the President.

stem: What is true about the proceedings of the State legislature?

options.label: a
options.text: Advocate General has right to vote

options.label: b
options.text: Business in the legisiature shall be transacted only in official language of the state or in Hindi or in English.

options.label: c
options.text: It can discuss the conduct of any judge of the High Court also

options.label: d
options.text: Validity of proceedings shall be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity

expl: Article 210(1) of the Indian Constitution provides that business in the State Legislature shall be transacted in the official language(s) of the State, or in Hindi, or in English. Hence, statement (b) is true. Under Article 177, the Advocate-General may take part in the proceedings of the State Legislature, but he does not have the right to vote. Under Article 211, the State Legislature cannot discuss the conduct of a Judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court in the discharge of his duties. Under Article 212(1), the validity of proceedings in the State Legislature cannot be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure.
